sources.title: Suspension of Visa Issuance to Foreign Nationals to Protect the Security of the United States
sources.officialityEvidence: The State Department's live PP 10998 implementation notice, last updated February 2, 2026, names the Republic of the Congo in the fully suspended nationality cohort and preserves exceptions and valid-visa grandfathering.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Afghanistan, Burma, Burkina Faso, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea

sources.title: 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38), geographical definition of United States
sources.publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives
sources.officialityEvidence: The official U.S. Code publication defines the United States for INA purposes to include Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands, and the Northern Mariana Islands.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands of the United States, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands

conflicts.explanation: The current full suspension preserves valid-visa grandfathering, specified exceptions and case-by-case waivers, so it cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes Puerto Rico. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes Guam. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes the Northern Mariana Islands. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
The full suspension is an INA entry and visa-issuance rule; the INA geographical definition includes the U.S. Virgin Islands. Its exceptions cannot be flattened to a normal visitor status.
